intro: Talk about films and books: genres, plots, opinions, dubbing, subtitles and recommendations.
p.protagonista.consejo: It works for a man and a woman: «el protagonista», «la protagonista». The ending does not change.
p.personaje.consejo: It is masculine: «el personaje», even if the character is a woman.
p.argumento.consejo: It is also a reason to defend an idea. In a film it is the story.
p.tratar de.consejo: The film «trata de» a topic: «¿De qué trata?». With an infinitive, «tratar de» means to try.
p.ciencia ficción.consejo: It tells imagined futures, spaceships or robots: «una película de ciencia ficción».
p.versión original.consejo: You say «en versión original» and it usually has subtitles. It is abbreviated «V. O.».
p.doblada.consejo: It changes with the noun: «película doblada», «series dobladas». The noun is «doblaje».
p.final.consejo: Careful: «el final» is the last part; «la final» is the last match of a competition.
p.cartelera.consejo: A film is «en cartelera» while it is shown in cinemas. It comes from «cartel».
p.taquilla.consejo: The ll sounds like y: ta-KI-ya. There you buy the ticket for the cinema or theatre.
p.recomendar.consejo: The e becomes ie: «recomiendo», «recomienda», but «recomendamos». It takes the subjunctive: «te recomiendo que veas».
p.merece la pena.consejo: It goes with an infinitive: «merece la pena verla». It is a fixed expression; its opposite is «no merece la pena».
p.estrenar.glosa: to premiere; to use for the first time
p.estrenar.consejo: A film «se estrena» on its first day. You also «estrenar» new clothes when you wear them for the first time.
p.subtítulos.consejo: In the cinema it is almost always plural: «con subtítulos». They appear at the bottom of the screen.
b1.titulo: Talking about a film or book
b1.texto:
Genres: **una película de terror**, **de risa**, **de amor**, **de acción** or **de ciencia ficción**; **una novela policíaca**, **histórica** or **de aventuras**.

The plot is told in the present: **trata de** a woman who **busca** her son; the protagonist **es** a detective who **vive** in Barcelona.

You can watch a film **en versión original**, **subtitulada** or **doblada**. Those adjectives agree with **película**.

Give your opinion: **me encantó**; **está muy bien**; **es un rollo**; **tiene un final abierto**; **merece la pena**; **no merece la pena**.

To advise, **recomendar que** takes the subjunctive: **te recomiendo que la veas**; **te aconsejo que leas** the book first. **Tienes que verla** is a stronger recommendation.

A film **se estrena** and **está en cartelera**; tickets are bought at **la taquilla**.
b2.f0.texto: Have you seen that director's latest film?
b2.f1.texto: I have not seen it yet.
b2.f3.texto: It is about a journalist who discovers a secret of her family.
b2.f6.texto: No, it is a drama with an open ending.
b2.f8.texto: I recommend that you watch it in the original version with subtitles.
b2.f9.texto: Is it still on at the cinemas?
b4.texto:
Three structures to talk about stories:

- **Tratar de** + topic: **La película trata de una periodista.** To ask: **¿De qué trata?**
- **Recomendar que** / **aconsejar que** + subjunctive: **Te recomiendo que la veas.** Stronger: **Tienes que verla.**
- **Merece la pena** + infinitive: **Merece la pena verla.** The opposite: **No merece la pena.**

To describe a character or a plot, use **que** + present: **una película que hace pensar**.
b4.e0.texto: The novel is about a detective who lives in Barcelona.
b4.e1.texto: I advise you to read the book first.
b4.e2.texto: It is worth watching it in the original version.
b5.f0.texto: The cinema hall is dark and smells of warm popcorn.
b5.f1.texto: The lights go out little by little.
b5.f2.texto: On the screen appears the sea under a stormy sky.
b5.f3.texto: A young woman walks alone along an empty beach.
b5.f4.texto: Lucía and Pablo watch the scene without blinking.
b5.f5.texto: The main character opens an old letter with trembling hands.
b5.f6.texto: Her soft voice tells an old family secret.
b5.f7.texto: In the hall nobody moves or breathes.
b5.f9.texto: On leaving, the two discuss the open ending under the street lights.
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Tratar con» means dealing with someone. Here «de» is used.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Tratar en» does not work to ask for the topic.
b7.o0.refuerzo: «Subtitulada» has written text but keeps the original voices.
b7.o1.refuerzo: That is it! «Doblada» means replacing the original voices.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Estrenada» is about the first day in cinemas, not about voices.
b7.pregunta: A foreign film with Spanish voices is...
b8.frase: Te recomiendo que la veas en versión original
b8.traduccion: I recommend you watch it in the original version
b9.o0.refuerzo: The «cartelera» is the list of films; it does not sell tickets.
b9.o1.refuerzo: The plot is the story of the film, not a place.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Well done! The «taquilla» is where tickets are sold.
b9.pregunta: Where do you buy the cinema ticket?
b10.frase: Te recomiendo que ____ el libro primero.
b10.o0.refuerzo: Well done! After «recomiendo que» comes the subjunctive: «leas».
b10.o1.refuerzo: «Lees» is the ordinary present: it does not express advice.
b10.o2.refuerzo: The infinitive does not work after «que».
b12.o0.refuerzo: That is it! Something that «merece la pena» is worth what it costs.
b12.o1.refuerzo: «Pena» is not sadness here. The expression is fixed.
b12.o2.refuerzo: «Pena» can also be a punishment, but this expression means «worth it».
b13.o0.refuerzo: «Doblar» is changing the voices, not starting to be shown.
b13.o1.refuerzo: Yes! A film «se estrena» on its first day in cinemas.
b13.o2.refuerzo: To recommend is to give advice; it does not mark the first day.
b13.pregunta: Which verb shows the first day in the cinema?
p.secreto.consejo: Something you keep hidden from others.
p.terror.consejo: A feeling of great fear, like in a scary film.
p.drama.consejo: A film or story with a serious, sad tone.
p.veas.consejo: From «ver», to see or watch. The «v» sounds like «b».
p.detective.consejo: Someone who looks for clues to solve a mystery.
p.palomitas.consejo: A snack eaten at the cinema.
p.pestañear.consejo: Opening and closing your eyes quickly.
p.temblorosas.consejo: Hands that shake a little, from nerves or cold.
p.imagen.consejo: What you see on a screen or in a picture.
p.esfuerzo.consejo: Work that takes energy and patience.
p.estrena.consejo: From «estrenar», to show something for the first time.
